Schedule relief is the appropriate remedy; if any monetary amount is unavoidable it must be capped at three months' Fees.

ops.newText: 7.6 If Customer's delay in providing an agreed dependency actually delays Vendor's performance, Vendor's sole remedy is a reasonable, equitable extension of the affected timeline, and Customer shall not be liable for liquidated damages, penalties, or other charges in respect of that delay.
ops.oldText: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.

proposal.summary: An uncapped daily liquidated-damages charge against us, triggered by any dependency delay, is unacceptable and could exceed the contract value. We have deleted it; Vendor's remedy is relief from affected timelines, and any unavoidable fee should be capped at three months' Fees.

ops.newText: 22.1 No more than once in any twelve-month period and on at least thirty days' prior written notice, Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services during normal business hours through an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations. Vendor and its auditor shall have no direct or remote access to Customer's systems, and the audit shall be conducted off-site wherever practicable and so as to minimise disruption to Customer's operations.
ops.oldText: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.

We have limited audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, via an independent auditor, with no system access; the cost-allocation in 22.2 already matches our position.

We have made this mutual, limited it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months, removed the no-hire ("engage") element and added the standard general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. ops.newText: 12.4 During the term and for twelve months after the end of a person's involvement in the Services, neither Party will solicit for employment any of the other Party's personnel who were directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This Section does not restrict general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at the other Party's personnel, or the hiring of a person who approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis, and neither Party is subject to any no-hire restriction.
ops.oldText: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.

We have narrowed it to our fallback: mutual, personnel involved in the Services, 12 months, with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
